verdict: Pentair sales fell 4% to $976M as Pool sales dropped 18% while channel partners worked through inventory, but Flow and Water Solutions grew and the quarter still earned $145M.

segments.name: Flow
segments.note: Pumps and flow products for residential, commercial and industrial water — sales up 4% (core sales up 1%), with segment income of $69M.

segments.name: Water Solutions
segments.note: Water treatment and filtration, including Everpure and Manitowoc Ice — sales up 1%, segment income up 16% to $121M at a 28.7% margin.

segments.name: Pool
segments.note: Pool pumps, filters and automation — sales down 18% as major channel partners finished realigning inventory; segment income fell 38% to $72M.

segments.name: Corporate and other
segments.note: Corporate and other sales — a rounding-sized remainder.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Selling and back-office costs — $176M, or 18.0% of sales, up from 15.9% a year ago as sales fell.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Developing new water products — $23M, about 2.4% of sales.

otherDetail: Net interest expense of $22M plus $1M of other expense — $23M taken out of profit.

takeaways.title: Pool was the whole decline
takeaways.text: Pool sales fell 18% to $292M and segment income fell 38% to $72M as channel partners completed an inventory realignment ahead of the 2027 pool season. Pentair guides Q4 sales up 7–9%.

takeaways.title: Water Solutions got more profitable
takeaways.text: Water Solutions income rose 16% to $121M — a 28.7% return on sales, up 3.7 points — and Flow income rose 15% to $69M. The two growing segments cushioned Pool.

takeaways.title: Adjusted profit vs GAAP profit
takeaways.text: GAAP operating income was $196M (20.1% of sales). Excluding $46M of restructuring, transformation, amortization and deal costs, adjusted operating income was $242M (24.8%).

oneTimers: Adjustments between GAAP and adjusted results were $46M before tax: $11M restructuring and other, $16M transformation costs, $15M intangible amortization, and $3M of deal costs for the Taco acquisition (closed October 1, after quarter-end).
Results include about $8M of IEEPA (tariff) refunds in the quarter — a benefit that is not part of normal product sales.
